question:
Agnes writes the following four statements on a blank piece of paper.

• At least one of these statements is true.

• At least two of these statements are true.

• At least two of these statements are false.

• At least one of these statements is false.

Each statement is either true or false. How many false statements did Agnes write on the paper?
solution:
The third statement is a useful starting point: if it is true, then the fourth statement must also be true.

Suppose the third statement is true. It claims that at least two statements are false, so the fourth statement, which claims at least one is false, is true as well. We now have two true statements, the third and fourth. This makes both the first and second statements true. But then all four statements are true, contradicting the third statement's claim that at least two are false.

Therefore the third statement is false. Its claim of at least two false statements fails, so there is at most one false statement. Since the third statement itself is false, there is exactly one.

This is consistent: with three true statements and one false statement, the first, second, and fourth claims are all true. The answer is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
